date_conflict: OPEN CONFLICT, RECORDED AND NOT RESOLVED. Two Saudi instruments bear on IFRS 18 and they are NOT the same kind of instrument. (a) The Saudi Organization for Chartered and Professional Accountants (SOCPA) adopted IFRS 18 for application in the Kingdom on 2024-12-26 (Accounting Standards Council resolution 25/06/1446H), which is the local adoption instrument. (b) The Capital Market Authority announcement CMA_N_4083 of 2026-06-30 is the Board's decision on EARLY ADOPTION during 2026; it states that mandatory application commences for financial reporting periods beginning on or after 2027-01-01. research/specification_v1.2.md section 1.2 recorded T-A as 2026-06-30, which is date (b), an early-adoption decision, not the instrument that makes IFRS 18 mandatory. The registered rule (condition 2) asks for the instrument MAKING IFRS 18 MANDATORY, so T-A is 2024-12-26 and date (b) is recorded as a separate event. CONSEQUENCE THAT MUST NOT BE DISCOVERED LATE: CMA_N_4083 also requires a preliminary assessment of the expected impact of initial application in approved financial statements for periods beginning on or after 2026-04-01. With T-A at 2024-12-26 that mandated pre-adoption disclosure falls INSIDE the transition window rather than before it, so Saudi Arabia does not have the clean pre-disclosure anchor T-PRE that research/specification_v1.2.md section 2 requires of PH-1. Whether the Saudi row enters PH-1 at all, and on what footing, is a decision that must be made BEFORE the holdout is opened and must not be settled by looking at outcomes.
